"I have been speaking with Gil since we arrived on this island. Every morning I would wake with a supply of Sandiberries. We spoke often about things, such as morality, and duty. Now that he is gone. I wish I had spent more time talking about things, like love, and care. This island is difficult. It is easy to become swamped in the pain. But we cannot. We have no choice but to move forward together. It will be exceptionally difficult, and dreadfully unfair. 

If there is one thing Gil taught me. It is that service is **never** fair. The petty squabbles must end. Knights, Masons, townsfolk, workers, merchants, aristocrats, council members. None of these titles matter. What matters is who we are. We are all ***SURVIVORS***. This is not the end of our town, rather the beginning of our redemption. I love you all."

May your spirit never grow lonely, grow cold. May the Oasis be everything you imagined, be all the solace you knew it could be. I promise you that we will not forget you. I promise your plants, all here in the oasis will be taken care of. We will be together, even though it is together without you. You were better than we were, and it is not right that you died for it. You deserved better than this. I swear to you now, with all the strength I have left, that those who defiled your body as such will wish they never touched a single scale. Rest long and well friend."
